title: Reflect
coreMove: Turn today's evidence into one small adjustment for tomorrow instead of judging the whole system by mood.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar links Reflect to a small scientific-method loop: notice what worked and failed, then refine, add, or drop tactics without turning reflection into formal analytics.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong generic version says journal about productivity or track every habit. The specific move is to make one evidence-based adjustment to the next Make Time attempt.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

tryThisNow: rate your day from one to ten
write three things that went well

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: a ceramics kiln technician adjusting glaze-test timing
exampleSpecs.audience: a craft operator who needs evidence rather than self-blame after a failed firing
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next batch clouds again if the failed timing is repeated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes worked, failed, and change beside the test tiles, drops the late-night loading tactic, and refines tomorrow's firing start by thirty minutes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three cloudy glaze tiles cooling on a wire rack

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender revising arraignment prep after a chaotic morning
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer who needs to learn from a bad setup without redesigning the whole practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: tomorrow's client interview starts late again if the broken prep order is repeated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he chooses one adjustment: add a printed docket pull before hallway calls, while keeping the Highlight and Laser tactics that worked
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded arraignment docket beside a courthouse security bin receipt

exampleSpecs.domain: a robotics club mentor reviewing a failed sensor calibration session
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coach teaching students to treat tactics as experiments
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team wastes another build night if the calibration setup is blamed vaguely
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the students which Laser barrier worked and which setup failed, then writes add a parts tray as tomorrow's single experiment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a small distance sensor blinking beside a pile of loose screws

exampleSpecs.domain: a farmers market gate supervisor testing a new shopper-count routine
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead who needs quick learning without a heavy dashboard
exampleSpecs.stakes: the market misprices stall fees again if the count routine is kept only because it sounded efficient
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, he keeps the routine because he invented it; after, he checks two notes, drops the clipboard handoff, and adds a click counter at the narrowest entrance
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a click counter resting beside a chalkboard stall map before opening

exampleSpecs.domain: a community radio producer refining a morning interview block
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer who must separate a rough day from a bad method
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next guest gets rushed if the intro prep keeps sliding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she notes that the Highlight was right but the Laser setup failed, refines the guest-prep cue sheet, and drops the open newsroom chat for tomorrow's first block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marked guest-prep cue sheet beside a red on-air light

exampleSpecs.domain: a printmaking studio lead improving a volunteer open-studio plan
exampleSpecs.audience: a studio coordinator who needs a light feedback loop after mixed results
exampleSpecs.stakes: volunteers spend another Saturday setting up the wrong stations if the lesson is not captured
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts the station staging was the failure, checks the ink-stained sign-in sheet against finished prints, and writes drop extra brayers, add drying labels for next time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: ink-stained gloves lying beside a rack of unfinished prints

skillTargets: turn a rough day into one refine, add, or drop decision
distinguish evidence-based reflection from mood-based self-judgment
analyze which part of the Make Time loop failed under real conditions
evaluate when tracking has become heavier than the adjustment it is supposed to support

tryThisNowSpec: Write three short labels for today: worked, failed, change. Under change, write only one refine, add, or drop decision that would improve tomorrow.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm -- a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
